Requirement: All tailoring shall be evaluated for use by the KSC Engineering Directorate Technical Authority (see KSC-PLN-5400).
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'evaluated for use' is not testable.
How to verify: Inspect the generated evaluation report against the criteria specified in KSC-PLN-5400.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall provide an evaluation report for all tailoring items as defined in KSC-PLN-5400.

Requirement: Waivers to institutional requirements shall follow the process in KDP-KSC-P-1865.
Model issues: The requirement uses 'shall follow the process in KDP-KSC-P-1865,' which is an instruction to follow a procedure rather than a verifiable system behavior.
How to verify: Inspect the system documentation and process flow to confirm adherence to KDP-KSC-P-1865.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall implement the waiver process as defined in KDP-KSC-P-1865.

Requirement: Conflicts between this standard and applicable documents cited herein shall be resolved by the responsible Technical Authorities.
Model issues: The requirement delegates resolution authority without defining the resolution process or criteria, making it untestable.
How to verify: Review the system design against all cited documents to confirm adherence to the most stringent requirement in case of conflict.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall adhere to the most stringent requirement when conflicts exist between this standard and applicable documents cited herein.

Requirement: COTS equipment shall be evaluated for acceptability from a materials and processes (M&P) standpoint (see 6).
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'acceptability' needs a measurable criterion.
How to verify: Inspect the evaluation report to confirm that COTS equipment was assessed against the criteria listed in section 6.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall evaluate COTS equipment for M&P acceptability according to the criteria defined in section 6.

Requirement: Qualification tests and inspections shall be indicated in the engineering documentation.
Model issues: The term 'indicated' is vague; it needs to specify *how* the indication must occur (e.g., via a specific field, checklist, or document section).
How to verify: Review the engineering documentation to confirm that records for all qualification tests and inspections are present.
Suggested rewrite: The engineering documentation shall include a record of all qualification tests and inspections.

Requirement: Vendor documentation shall be provided as evidence that the requirements of this standards manual have been met.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; it does not specify *what* documentation is required or *how* it must be provided.
How to verify: Review the submitted vendor documentation against the requirements listed in the standards manual.
Suggested rewrite: The vendor shall provide documentation demonstrating compliance with the requirements of this standards manual.

Requirement: Modifications to COTS shall be performed in accordance with this standards manual.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject performing the action.
How to verify: Inspect the modification documentation to confirm adherence to the standards manual.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall perform modifications to COTS in accordance with this standards manual.

Requirement: The GS design shall support the program/project-specific operational requirements of flight hardware.
Model issues: The requirement is too high-level and lacks specific, testable criteria regarding what 'support' means in this context.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation against the referenced operational requirements document.
Suggested rewrite: The GS design shall support the operational requirements of flight hardware as defined in <<document reference>>.

Requirement: GS shall not degrade or contaminate flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments while it is being used, checked out, serviced, or otherwise handled.
Model issues: The terms 'degrade' and 'contaminate' are not quantitatively measurable without further definition.
How to verify: Measure the specified parameters (e.g., signal integrity, particulate count) of the affected systems before and after GS interaction to confirm no degradation or contamination occurred.
Suggested rewrite:
GS shall not cause any measurable degradation to flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments during use, checkout, servicing, or handling.
GS shall not introduce any measurable contamination to flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments during use, checkout, servicing, or handling.

Requirement: GS design shall include access provisions for handling, servicing, calibrating, maintaining, and replacing components and limited-life items.
Model issues: The scope of 'access provisions' is not defined, making verification difficult.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation and physical prototype to confirm the presence and adequacy of access provisions as defined by <<specific access criteria>>.
Suggested rewrite: The GS design shall provide access provisions for handling, servicing, calibrating, maintaining, and replacing components and limited-life items, such that <<specific access criteria>> is met.

Requirement: GS shall meet the requirements of all interfaces with new or existing hardware or software as documented in interface control documents (ICDs) or any other documentation that controls interface requirements.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it should specify *which* interfaces or *what* aspect of the ICDs must be met.
How to verify: Review the ICDs and compare the documented interface requirements against the GS design documentation.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall meet the interface requirements documented in the Interface Control Documents (ICDs) for all specified hardware and software interfaces.

Requirement: Fluid, mechanical, or electrical connections in close proximity shall be designed to prevent cross-connections.
Model issues: The term 'close proximity' is not quantified, making verification impossible.
How to verify: Inspect the design drawings to confirm that all connections within the specified proximity adhere to the cross-connection prevention design.
Suggested rewrite: Fluid, mechanical, or electrical connections shall be designed to prevent cross-connections when located within <<distance>>, and the design shall be verifiable via inspection.

Requirement: GS shall be compatible with all facility interfaces.
Model issues: The term 'compatible' is not verifiable without defining the specific interface protocols or standards.
How to verify: Inspect the interface control documents to confirm adherence to specified protocols for each facility interface.
Suggested rewrite:
GS shall interface with Facility Interface A using <<protocol>>.
GS shall interface with Facility Interface B using <<protocol>>.

Requirement: GS shall be designed for the operational life specified by program or mission requirements and identified in design drawings and maintenance documents.
Model issues: The requirement defers to external documents ('program or mission requirements', 'design drawings and maintenance documents') without specifying the required life, making it untestable as written.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the specified operational life requirement is documented and traceable.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall be designed for an operational life of <<specified operational life>>.

Requirement: Existing GS that was verified to meet the GS requirements of a previous NASA program shall be considered acceptable for use without further verification to the requirements of this standards manual.
Model issues: The term 'acceptable' is not measurable and needs to be replaced with a specific condition for acceptance.
How to verify: Inspect the documentation to confirm the previous verification against the NASA program requirements meets the specified acceptance condition.
Suggested rewrite: Existing GS verified to meet the GS requirements of a previous NASA program shall be accepted for use without further verification to the requirements of this standards manual if <<specific condition for acceptance>> is met.

Requirement: Items with limited life shall be identified on design drawings and annotated with the specific limitation to the life of the item.
Model issues: The term 'limited life' is not defined and needs a measurable criterion.
How to verify: Inspect the design drawings to confirm that all items with a defined limited life are marked and annotated with the specific limitation.
Suggested rewrite:
Items with a defined limited life shall be identified on design drawings.
Each identified item shall be annotated with its specific life limitation.

Requirement: The colors in Appendix A shall be used for GS designed and painted for NASA/KSC.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject (what 'shall be used' implies) and needs to specify the action or condition under which the colors must be used.
How to verify: Inspect the design and painted GS against the color specifications listed in Appendix A.
Suggested rewrite: The GS shall utilize the colors specified in Appendix A when designed and painted for NASA/KSC.

Requirement: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall be physically oriented or separated such that the failure of one will not prevent the other from performing its intended function.
Model issues: The term 'physically oriented or separated' is too vague to define a pass/fail criterion.
How to verify: Measure the physical distance between the redundant components and confirm it meets the specified separation distance.
Suggested rewrite: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall maintain a physical separation distance of at least <<separation distance>> to prevent single-point failure propagation.

Requirement: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall be designed such that common- cause failures (e.g., contamination) do not eliminate redundancy.
Model issues: The term 'eliminate redundancy' is not precisely measurable; it needs a defined failure mode or metric.
How to verify: Analyze the design documentation to confirm that failure modes related to contamination do not result in the loss of redundant function.
Suggested rewrite: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall be designed to prevent common-cause failures (e.g., contamination) from causing the loss of redundancy capability.

Requirement: The design of redundant systems shall provide methods for verifying each redundant element without compromising the reliability of the redundant system.
Model issues: The term 'methods for verifying' is too vague; specify the required verification mechanism or criteria.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm the specified verification mechanism meets the stated criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The design shall provide a mechanism to verify each redundant element without compromising the reliability of the redundant system.

Requirement: GS, except primary structure and pressure vessels/piping/tubing in rupture mode, shall be designed to sustain a failure without causing loss of life or damage to support equipment, facilities, or flight hardware (fail-safe).
Model issues: The term 'fail-safe' is not defined or quantified, making the requirement untestable.
How to verify: Analyze the design documentation against the defined fail-safe criteria.
Suggested rewrite: GS, except primary structure and pressure vessels/piping/tubing in rupture mode, shall be designed to sustain a failure without causing loss of life or damage to support equipment, facilities, or flight hardware, meeting the defined fail-safe criteria.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to sustain a failure and still perform its basic function (fail- operational) when necessary to meet safety or operational requirements.
Model issues: The term 'sustain a failure' is too vague; specify the type or magnitude of failure that must be sustained.
How to verify: Induce the specified failure mode and verify that GS continues to perform its basic function.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall maintain basic function when a specified failure mode occurs to meet safety or operational requirements.

Requirement: GS failure modes/inadvertent operator actions with the potential for loss of flight crew shall be addressed in accordance with NPR 8705.2.
Model issues: The requirement is too high-level; it mandates compliance with a document but doesn't specify the required system behavior.
How to verify: Inspect the system design documentation to confirm that all specified failure modes and operator actions are addressed per NPR 8705.2.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall address GS failure modes and inadvertent operator actions with the potential for loss of flight crew in accordance with NPR 8705.2.

Requirement: GS shall be designed such that failures will not be propagated to the flight systems.
Model issues: The term 'failures' is too broad; it needs to specify the type or source of failure being prevented.
How to verify: Analyze the system architecture and failure modes to confirm that the specified failure type cannot propagate to the flight systems.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall prevent the propagation of <<specific failure type>> to the flight systems.

Requirement: A criticality assessment shall be performed early in the design phase to determine the need for performing a reliability and/or safety analysis.
Rule findings: and/or: and/or; passive voice: shall be performed
Model issues: The term 'early in the design phase' is not specific enough for verification.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm the criticality assessment was performed by the specified milestone.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall perform a criticality assessment by <<date/milestone>> to determine the need for performing a reliability analysis or a safety analysis.

Requirement: System inputs (including dependencies such as electrical power and pneumatic purges) and outputs (including all control and monitoring functions) that could fail with potentially catastrophic or critical consequences shall be identified as reliability critical (FMEA is required).
Rule findings: open-ended list: such as; absolute: all
Model issues: The requirement bundles identification, classification, and process mandate (FMEA).
How to verify: Review the system design documentation and FMEA report to confirm all critical items are identified and marked.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall identify all inputs and outputs that could fail with potentially catastrophic or critical consequences.
These identified inputs and outputs shall be designated as reliability critical.
An FMEA shall be performed on all reliability critical components.

Requirement: Systems with hazards to personnel or equipment during normal or credible use scenarios shall be identified as critical (Hazard Analysis is required).
Model issues: The term 'normal' needs to be quantified or replaced with a defined operational state.
How to verify: Review the hazard analysis documentation to confirm that all systems with hazards during defined operational scenarios are marked as critical.
Suggested rewrite: Systems with hazards to personnel or equipment during defined operational scenarios shall be identified as critical (Hazard Analysis is required).

Requirement: An FMEA shall be performed in accordance with program-defined methodology on those systems and subsystems identified by the criticality analysis as having the potential to cause a criticality 1, 1S, 1R, or 2 condition.
Model issues: The requirement implies a process ('shall be performed') rather than a verifiable system state, and 'program-defined methodology' is too vague without reference.
How to verify: Inspect the FMEA documentation to confirm it was performed on the correct systems and followed the specified methodology.
Suggested rewrite: An FMEA shall be performed on systems and subsystems identified by the criticality analysis as having the potential to cause a criticality 1, 1S, 1R, or 2 condition, following the methodology specified in <<Methodology Document ID>>.

Requirement: Based on the results of the FMEA, components having failure modes that could cause an undesirable event (other than criticality 3) shall be identified, categorized, and approved in accordance with the applicable agency, program, or KSC requirements.
Model issues: The requirement bundles identification, categorization, and approval into one statement.; The term 'undesirable event' is not defined or measurable.
How to verify: Review the FMEA documentation to confirm the identification of components based on the specified criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall identify components whose failure modes could cause an undesirable event (excluding criticality 3).

Requirement: In the absence of a program requirement, the methodology of KNPR 8700.2 shall be used.
Model issues: The phrase 'In the absence of a program requirement' creates a conditional dependency that is not fully defined for verification.
How to verify: Inspect the system documentation to confirm the methodology used when no program requirement is present.
Suggested rewrite: If no program requirement is specified, the system shall use the methodology defined in KNPR 8700.2.

Requirement: The criticality categories shown in Table 1 shall be used when the program does not identify categories.
Model issues: Table 1 must be referenced to define the criticality categories.
How to verify: Inspect the system documentation to confirm the use of Table 1 categories when program identification fails.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall use the criticality categories defined in Table 1 when the program does not identify categories.

Requirement: Static components, such as pressure vessels, pressure lines, cables, connectors, and wiring, shall be considered only if failure can be attributed to an active component failure.
Model issues: The requirement is conditional and unclear about the scope of 'considered' (e.g., design review, testing, maintenance).; The condition ('if failure can be attributed to an active component failure') is subjective and not testable.
How to verify: Review the failure attribution documentation to confirm that static components are only analyzed when an active component failure is the root cause.
Suggested rewrite: Static components shall be excluded from failure attribution analysis unless the failure is demonstrably caused by an active component failure.

Requirement: A Hazard Analysis shall be performed on those systems and subsystems determined by the criticality assessment to be a potential threat to flight systems, ground systems, or safety.
Model issues: The term 'potential threat' is vague and needs a measurable criterion for inclusion in the analysis scope.
How to verify: Inspect the criticality assessment and the Hazard Analysis report to confirm the scope matches the defined criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The Hazard Analysis shall be performed on systems and subsystems identified by the criticality assessment as having a criticality level of <<criticality level>> or higher, where criticality level is defined in <<document reference>>.

Requirement: Based on the results of the Hazard Analysis, those hazards that could not be eliminated by design or mitigated to an acceptable level shall require a Hazard Report.
Model issues: The term 'acceptable level' needs a quantifiable threshold or reference to a specific standard.
How to verify: Review the Hazard Analysis and verify that a Hazard Report is generated for all hazards exceeding the defined risk level.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall require a Hazard Report for any hazard that cannot be eliminated by design or mitigated to a risk level of <<acceptable risk level>>.

Requirement: FMEA and/or Hazard Analysis including the results of the analysis shall be combined into a Systems Assurance Analysis (SAA) to summarize the risks resulting from each system/subsystem analysis.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two actions: combining analyses and summarizing risks.
How to verify: Review the final SAA document to confirm it contains the combined results from the FMEA and Hazard Analysis.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall combine the FMEA and Hazard Analysis results into a Systems Assurance Analysis (SAA).
Each system/subsystem analysis shall contribute its resulting risks to the SAA.

Requirement: CIL and Hazard Reports shall be approved and maintained as part of the design documentation.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific action or condition for approval/maintenance, making it hard to test.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the presence and approval status of the CIL and Hazard Reports.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall ensure CIL and Hazard Reports are approved and maintained within the design documentation.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to perform in the natural and induced environments to which it will be subjected during its life cycle.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'natural and induced environments' must be specified or referenced.
How to verify: Subject the GS to the environmental conditions defined in the specified document and verify operational correctness.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall operate correctly when subjected to the environmental conditions specified in <<Environmental Specification Document>>.

Requirement: GS used or stored in an uncontrolled exterior environment shall be designed to function after exposure to the natural environment at its respective geographical location as specified in NASA-HDBK-1001.
Model issues: The phrase 'designed to function after exposure' is vague; it needs a specific performance metric or operational state to verify functionality.
How to verify: Subject the GS to environmental conditions specified in NASA-HDBK-1001 and verify that it maintains specified operational performance.
Suggested rewrite: GS used or stored in an uncontrolled exterior environment shall maintain specified operational performance after exposure to the natural environment conditions defined in NASA-HDBK-1001.

Requirement: GS required to function during or after exposure to the launch-induced environment shall be designed to withstand the environment defined in program-specific documents.
Model issues: The phrase 'shall be designed to withstand' is too broad; it needs a specific design criterion or testable threshold.
How to verify: Subject the GS to the launch-induced environment defined in program-specific documents and verify that it maintains full functionality.
Suggested rewrite: The GS shall maintain full functionality when exposed to the launch-induced environment defined in program-specific documents.

Requirement: Testing of GS for launch-induced environment shall be applied in accordance with KSC-STD-164.
Model issues: The requirement is passive and lacks a clear subject performing the action.
How to verify: Inspect the test plan to confirm adherence to KSC-STD-164 for GS launch environment testing.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall test GS for launch-induced environment in accordance with KSC-STD-164.

Requirement: GS not required to function after exposure to the launch-induced environment shall not cause damage or create a hazard to flight hardware, facilities, other GS, personnel, or the environment.
Model issues: The requirement bundles multiple distinct safety/damage prevention criteria (damage to hardware, facilities, other GS, personnel, environment) into one statement.; The term 'damage' is not quantifiable.
How to verify: Analyze the system design and failure modes against the defined launch-induced environment to confirm no hazardous outputs or damage mechanisms exist.
Suggested rewrite:
The GS shall not cause damage to flight hardware when exposed to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to facilities when exposed to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to other GS when exposed to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to personnel when exposed to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to the environment when exposed to the launch-induced environment.

Requirement: GS designed to function within a controlled interior environment shall be designed to the following temperature and humidity requirements:
Model issues: The requirement lacks specific numerical values for the temperature and humidity limits.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the specified operating temperature and humidity ranges.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall operate within a controlled interior environment where the temperature shall be between <<min temp>> and <<max temp>> and the relative humidity shall be between <<min humidity>> and <<max humidity>>.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to meet the program/project contamination control requirements.
Model issues: The requirement defers to an external document ('program/project contamination control requirements') without specifying which one, making verification impossible without that document.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation against the specified contamination control requirements in <<document ID>>.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall meet the contamination control requirements specified in <<document ID>>.

Requirement: Clean rooms and associated controlled environments designated as GS shall be designed in accordance with ASTM E2217.
Model issues: The term 'designated as GS' is unclear; it should specify what 'GS' refers to.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm compliance with ASTM E2217 and the specified GS designation.
Suggested rewrite: Clean rooms and associated controlled environments shall be designed in accordance with ASTM E2217, and shall be designated as <<GS designation>>.

Requirement: GS used in an uncontrolled interior environment shall be designed to meet the most severe exterior environmental conditions for humidity and temperature expected at the respective geographical locations, as defined in NASA-HDBK-1001.
Model issues: The requirement uses 'shall be designed to meet' which is a design constraint, but the verification needs to confirm the design meets the standard, not just that it was designed to.; The phrase 'most severe exterior environmental conditions' is slightly vague; it should reference the specific conditions derived from the standard.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm compliance with the environmental specifications listed in NASA-HDBK-1001.
Suggested rewrite: The GS shall meet the humidity and temperature conditions specified in NASA-HDBK-1001 for the respective geographical locations.

Requirement: If GS will be operated in locations where fire or explosion hazards exist, as defined by NFPA 70, Article 500, it shall be hazardproofed in accordance with the requirements in KSC-STD-E-0002.
Model issues: The condition 'If GS will be operated in locations where fire or explosion hazards exist' is conditional and should be separated from the requirement itself.
How to verify: Inspect the GS documentation and physical installation against the requirements of KSC-STD-E-0002 when deployed in a hazardous location.
Suggested rewrite: When operated in locations defined by NFPA 70, Article 500, the GS shall be hazardproofed in accordance with KSC-STD-E-0002.

Requirement: Environmental methods and conditions required for testing and qualification of GS components shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-810 and KSC-STD-164.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm adherence to the specified military and Korean standards.
Suggested rewrite: Environmental methods and conditions required for testing and qualification of GS components shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-810 and KSC-STD-164.

Requirement: GS used in Zones 3 or 4 as defined in NASA-HDBK-1001 shall be designed to resist the effects of a seismic event using the criteria and guidelines in ASCE-7.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two concepts: the scope (GS used in Zones 3 or 4) and the design constraint (resist seismic event).; The phrase 'designed to resist' is not specific enough; it needs a measurable performance criterion derived from ASCE-7.
How to verify: Review the design documentation against the specific seismic design criteria outlined in ASCE-7 for the defined zones.
Suggested rewrite: GS used in Zones 3 or 4 shall meet the seismic design criteria specified in ASCE-7.

Requirement: Drawings and specifications required for the fabrication, construction, installation, modification, test, operation, maintenance, sustaining, and use of GS shall be prepared in accordance with drawing practices equal to or more stringent than the engineering drawing practices of ASME Y14.100 and KSC-GP-435, Vol.
Model issues: The requirement references an incomplete standard reference (Vol.)
How to verify: Inspect the documentation package to confirm adherence to the specified drawing practices.
Suggested rewrite: Drawings and specifications required for the fabrication, construction, installation, modification, test, operation, maintenance, sustaining, and use of GS shall be prepared in accordance with drawing practices equal to or more stringent than the engineering drawing practices of ASME Y14.100 and KSC-GP-435, Vol. <<Volume Number>>.

Requirement: Technical documentation (e.g., manuals and reports) shall be prepared in accordance with KSC-DF-107.
How to verify: Inspect the prepared documentation against the requirements specified in KSC-DF-107.
Suggested rewrite: Technical documentation shall be prepared in accordance with KSC-DF-107.

Requirement: GS design documentation shall identify spare parts, components, materials, and items necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
Model issues: The requirement bundles multiple distinct identification tasks (spare parts, components, materials, items) into one statement.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation to confirm the presence of identified lists for spare parts, components, materials, and items.
Suggested rewrite:
The GS design documentation shall identify spare parts necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify components necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify materials necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify items necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.

Requirement: Limited-life items shall be controlled from the date of their manufacture through their period of operational use, including the time they are in storage.
Model issues: The term 'controlled' is not defined; specify the required control mechanism (e.g., tracking, quarantine, usage logging).
How to verify: Inspect the item tracking records to confirm the required control mechanism was applied throughout the specified lifecycle.
Suggested rewrite: Limited-life items shall be tracked from the date of manufacture through their period of operational use, including storage time, using <<control mechanism>>.

Requirement: The status of limited-life items shall be documented.
Model issues: The requirement lacks specificity regarding what 'documented' means (e.g., format, location, required data fields).
How to verify: Inspect the <<documentation system>> to confirm that the status of all limited-life items is recorded.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall record the status of limited-life items in the <<documentation system>>.

Requirement: GS design documentation shall identify limited-life items and provide instructions for replacement of those parts, components, and materials.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct actions: identifying items and providing replacement instructions.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation to confirm the presence of a list of limited-life items and corresponding replacement procedures.
Suggested rewrite:
GS design documentation shall identify all limited-life items.
GS design documentation shall provide instructions for the replacement of identified limited-life parts, components, and materials.

Requirement: All components used in critical GS shall undergo qualification to verify performance in their intended environment in accordance with KSC-STD-G-0003.
Model issues: The term 'critical GS' is undefined and needs to be specified.
How to verify: Inspect the component qualification records to confirm adherence to KSC-STD-G-0003 for all components designated as critical GS.
Suggested rewrite: All components used in <<critical GS>> shall undergo qualification to verify performance in their intended environment in accordance with KSC-STD-G-0003.

Requirement: GS design shall incorporate quality requirements in accordance with the program’s/project’s S&MA Plan.
Model issues: The reference to 'program’s/project’s S&MA Plan' is too broad; the specific document or section must be cited.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation to confirm inclusion of requirements from the specified S&MA Plan.
Suggested rewrite: GS design shall incorporate quality requirements specified in the <<specific S&MA Plan document ID>>.

Requirement: Quality requirements shall be defined on the engineering drawings or in other technical documents that are included in the design, fabrication, or installation contract.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it states *where* quality requirements shall be defined rather than *what* the quality requirements are.
How to verify: Review the design, fabrication, and installation contracts to confirm the presence of a documented process for defining quality requirements.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall include a documented process for defining quality requirements in the engineering drawings or in other technical documents included in the design, fabrication, or installation contract.

Requirement: Certification documentation for required training of personnel performing processes during fabrication, assembly, installation, and testing of GS shall be maintained in accordance with KNPR 8730.2.
Model issues: The requirement implies a state ('shall be maintained') rather than an active capability, which is less direct for verification.
How to verify: Inspect the documentation repository to confirm the presence and adherence of training certifications to KNPR 8730.2.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall maintain certification documentation for personnel training related to fabrication, assembly, installation, and testing of GS in accordance with KNPR 8730.2.

Requirement: Testing requirements shall be specified in engineering documentation.
Model issues: The term 'engineering documentation' is too broad; specify which documents must contain the testing requirements.
How to verify: Inspect the specified engineering documentation to confirm the presence of testing requirements.
Suggested rewrite: Testing requirements shall be specified in the <<specific document type>>.

Requirement: Testing shall verify compliance with the applicable specifications and the ability of the GS to perform its required design functions.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct concepts: compliance verification and functional performance verification.; It is not specific enough to define what 'applicable specifications' are or how 'required design functions' are defined.
How to verify: Execute a test plan derived from the functional specification and inspect the resulting data against the interface control documents.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall comply with all documented interface control documents.
Testing shall demonstrate that the GS performs all functions defined in the functional specification.

Requirement: Test documentation, data, and results shall be produced, maintained, and archived in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and program or project requirements.
Model issues: The phrase 'program or project requirements' is too vague and needs to be specified or referenced.
How to verify: Inspect the documentation, data, and archive to confirm compliance with KNPR 8730.2 and the specified project requirements.
Suggested rewrite: Test documentation, data, and results shall be produced, maintained, and archived in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and the <<specific project requirements document>>.

Requirement: A load test shall be performed on all structural GSE (access platforms, workstands, etc.) and moveable or articulating GS structures except when the load test creates an unsafe condition or when analysis shows the load test will result in damage to the structure.
Rule findings: open-ended list: etc; absolute: all; passive voice: shall be performed
Model issues: The scope of 'structural GSE' and 'moveable or articulating GS structures' needs to be defined or referenced.; The condition for exemption ('when analysis shows the load test will result in damage to the structure') needs a defined threshold for 'damage'.
How to verify: Review the load test plan and associated analysis reports to confirm compliance with the defined scope and exemption criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall perform a load test on all defined structural GSE (access platforms, workstands, etc.) and moveable or articulating GS structures, unless the load test creates an unsafe condition or unless analysis demonstrates the load test will result in damage exceeding <<damage threshold>>.

Requirement: The minimum test load shall be 125% of the design or working load for GS not used for lifting.
Model issues: The term 'design or working load' needs to be defined or referenced to be verifiable.
How to verify: Apply the calculated minimum test load to the GS and verify the system operates without failure.
Suggested rewrite: The minimum test load shall be 125% of the <<design or working load>> for GS not used for lifting.

Requirement: Lifting devices and equipment shall be proofload tested in accordance with NASA-STD-8719.9.
How to verify: Inspect the test documentation to confirm that proofload testing was performed on all lifting devices and equipment according to NASA-STD-8719.9.
Suggested rewrite: Lifting devices and equipment shall be proofload tested in accordance with NASA-STD-8719.9.

Requirement: In the absence of design analysis, a load test of 8 times the safe working load shall satisfy the factor of safety requirements of this standards manual.
Model issues: The phrase 'In the absence of design analysis' is conditional and unclear regarding when this test must occur.
How to verify: Apply a load of 8 times the safe working load and measure the resulting factor of safety against the standards manual.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall satisfy the factor of safety requirements of this standards manual when subjected to a load test of 8 times the safe working load, provided design analysis is not performed.

Requirement: NDE for components and materials shall be in accordance with 6.4.14.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject for the action 'shall be in accordance with' (e.g., 'The NDE process shall...').
How to verify: Inspect the NDE documentation and procedures to confirm adherence to the criteria defined in 6.4.14.
